=== FIX-A LANDED — r23 date-difference-in-days canonical (insertion site: between r23:1098 and r23:1100) ===
New LEADING CANONICAL 'DAYS BETWEEN TWO DATES (and the column-scope discipline that goes with it)' inserted immediately after the completed-age `date_diff('year',...)` block (r23:1074-1098) and before the EXTRACT(EPOCH)/to_unixtime DO-NOT-WRITE block (was r23:1100). Block contents:
  • Keyword anchors: 'days between two dates', 'days since signup', 'time to first purchase in days', 'tenure in days', 'account age in days', 'elapsed days', 'how many days from X to Y', 'days a ticket stays open', 'days from signup to first purchase', 'days to convert', 'days until first event', 'days between event A and event B', 'lag in days', 'gap in days'.
  • ONE-FACT lead: Trino 467 has NO `date - date -> integer` operator (the operator table only lists `date - interval -> date`, `time - interval -> time`, `timestamp - interval -> timestamp`, `interval - interval -> interval`). The day count between two dates is computed exclusively with `date_diff('day', earlier, later) -> bigint`. Signature cited verbatim: `date_diff(unit, timestamp1, timestamp2)` returns `timestamp2 - timestamp1` (POSITIVE when timestamp2 is later — so the LATER date goes in the THIRD argument).
  • PREFERRED canonical SQL (the exact iter640 Q2 shape, FIXED): CTE `customer_first_purchase` projects `customer_id` + `date_diff('day', c.signup_date, MIN(o.order_date)) AS days_to_purchase`; outer query `SELECT approx_percentile(days_to_purchase, 0.5) AS median_days_to_first_purchase FROM customer_first_purchase WHERE days_to_purchase IS NOT NULL`. days_to_purchase is COMPUTED + PROJECTED in the CTE THEN referenced by name above.
  • Why-each-piece bullets explaining the argument order (signup earlier, MIN(order_date) later), the in-CTE projection rule, the approx_percentile median primitive (PERCENTILE_CONT/MEDIAN inoculation cross-link), and the defensive IS NOT NULL guard.
  • COLUMN-SCOPE-DISCIPLINE note explicitly tying the iter640 Q2 bug to the same class as iter635/iter636 share-of-subset final-assembly scope rule — a column referenced in the outer query MUST already be in the SELECT list of the CTE/subquery the outer query reads from. The iter640 Q2 CTE projected `customer_id, signup_date, first_purchase_date` but the outer query referenced `days_to_purchase` (never projected) — `Column 'days_to_purchase' cannot be resolved` at analyze time. Cross-link to the iter636 share-of-subset scope canonical in r07.
  • LEFT JOIN variant for 'include non-converters in the population' — projects signup_date + first_order_date (nullable) in the CTE, computes date_diff at the outer level where both columns are still in scope; also satisfies column-scope discipline. Adds COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE first_order_date IS NULL) AS never_converted alongside the median.
  • GENERALIZE table (5 rows): days-signup-to-first-purchase, ticket-open-days, days-since-last-login, account-age-days, days-between-consecutive-events-LAG. Each row gives the earlier arg, the later arg, and the date_diff expression.

=== DOCS-VERIFICATION FINDINGS (BEFORE writing) ===
(1) Trino 467 operator table at trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html — VERIFIED via WebFetch: the subtraction operators involving date/time/timestamp/interval are EXACTLY: `date - interval -> date`, `time - interval -> time`, `timestamp - interval -> timestamp`, `interval - interval -> interval`. There is NO `date - date -> integer` operator and NO `date - date -> bigint` operator. There is also no documented `date - date -> interval` operator (only `timestamp - timestamp -> interval` exists in some standards — and even that is not documented in Trino's operator table for these explicit forms). Therefore `CAST(first_purchase_date - signup_date AS bigint)` is INVALID Trino — the inner subtraction has no operator match.
(2) date_diff signature — VERIFIED at the same docs page: `date_diff(unit, timestamp1, timestamp2)` returns `timestamp2 - timestamp1` expressed in `unit`. Therefore the result is POSITIVE when `timestamp2` is later than `timestamp1` — i.e. the LATER date goes in the THIRD argument. Confirmed via direct WebFetch of trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html.
